newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees strong weekend shopper turnout.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees strong weekend shopper turnout.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said on Sunday it posted strong, broadly-based sales gains over the past weekend, with holiday shoppers choosing practical gifts and smaller luxury items for relatives and friends.
"It's shaping up to be a home and family-oriented Christmas," John Costello, senior executive vice president of marketing, told Reuters in an interview.
While Costello declined to release precise figures, he said sales were strong across most of the retailer's stores and geographic locations.
"In general, industry analysts are saying our 1996 sales will top 1995 sales," he said. "We had very strong holiday season in 1995 and are confident 1996 will be even better."
Popular items included camcorders, video cassette recorders and portable phones, the company said. Sales of tools and toolsets have also been very strong, it said.
"We are selling 50 Craftsman Robogrip pliers a minute," Costello said. Gemstones necklaces which formed a "y" shape at the throat were selling well too, he said.
"Through the weekend, same store sales have been solidly on plan," he said.
Costello said the company was also seein good results from its so-called softer line of goods, like clothing and accessories.
"There have been gains across the board in men and women's casual wear, shoes, cosmetics and fine jewelry," he said.
The gains were driven by pleasant shopping weather, Sear's breadth of product mix, extensive marketing and the company's fast service in stores, he said.

"The average consumer is time-stressed and looking for a place to meet all of his or her shopping needs quickly," Costello said. "Plus, this is great shopping weather -- not too cold and no major snowstorms."

Sales, while solid throughout the United States, were particularly buoyant in the southeastern and southwestern United States, Costello said. The company opened eight new stores in California during November, he said.
As an aside, Costello also said tire sales had been quite strong. "While you won't find tires under the tree, people are getting their cars ready for holiday travel," he said.
In 1995, Sears fourth-quarter sales accounted for $10.9 billion of its annual $34.9 billion sales and $455 million of its $1.8 billion in total net income.
